title: Webhook delivery API
goals: Send events to registered HTTPS callbacks.
design: POST /subscriptions registers a customer-owned public HTTPS URL; POST /events accepts a customer-scoped Idempotency-Key and returns 202 plus event_id. GET /events/{id} returns status only to the owning customer. Reject loopback and private IPs and revalidate DNS before delivery. Payloads are capped at 64 KiB. A worker sends JSON to the callback. Retry failed delivery forever until it succeeds. Retain events for 7 days; deduplicate submissions for 24 hours. The receiver should deduplicate event_id.
alternatives: Polling is simpler but increases notification delay.
A managed queue adds deployment overhead; start with a database-backed worker at 1000 events/day.
acceptance_tests: Submitting the same customer/key twice returns the original event ID.

summary: The proposal is understandable and identifies the small-service scope.
Two reliability and authenticity requirements are missing.

findings.evidence: Retry failed delivery forever until it succeeds.
findings.issue: Unlimited retries violate the explicit five-attempt budget.
findings.recommendation: Persist attempt counts and stop after 5 attempts or 24 hours.

findings.evidence: A worker sends JSON to the callback.
findings.issue: No outbound HMAC signing mechanism is described.
findings.recommendation: Define signing, signature headers, and receiver verification using the subscription secret.

title: Webhook delivery API
goals: Send events to registered HTTPS callbacks.
design: POST /subscriptions registers a customer-owned public HTTPS URL; POST /events accepts a customer-scoped Idempotency-Key and returns 202 plus event_id. GET /events/{id} returns status only to the owning customer. Reject loopback and private IPs and revalidate DNS before delivery. Payloads are capped at 64 KiB. A worker signs the raw JSON payload with HMAC-SHA256 using the per-subscription secret and sends the signature and event_id in headers. Receivers verify the signature against the raw body. Retry timeouts, 429, and 5xx with exponential backoff and jitter, up to 5 attempts within 24 hours; stop on other 4xx and mark terminal failures. Store the attempt count and next_attempt_at durably. Retain events for 7 days; deduplicate submissions for 24 hours. The receiver should deduplicate event_id.
alternatives: Polling is simpler but increases notification delay.
A managed queue adds deployment overhead; start with a database-backed worker at 1000 events/day.
risks: Keep signing secrets out of logs; rotate through overlapping key IDs.
A crashed worker may redeliver; receivers deduplicate event_id.
acceptance_tests: Submitting the same customer/key twice returns the original event ID.
Verify the signature against raw bytes; tampering must fail.
Simulate repeated 503 responses and prove the worker stops after 5 attempts.
Reject private callback destinations at registration and again at delivery.
